summary:
H.R. 7266, titled the “Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity Act,” amends section 40124 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (42 U.S.C. 18723) by striking the existing section and inserting a revised section 40124 to reauthorize and restructure the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program. The reauthorization expands the class of eligible entities, refines award criteria, establishes information-protection measures, and authorizes appropriations.

Subsection (a) adds statutory definitions. “Advanced cybersecurity technology” encompasses hardware, software, operational capabilities, or services improving electric utilities’ ability to protect against, detect, respond to, or recover from cybersecurity threats. “Eligible entity” is defined to include not only rural electric cooperatives, municipally owned electric utilities, and utility-owning political-subdivision instrumentalities, but also not-for-profit entities in partnership with at least six of the foregoing, and investor-owned electric utilities selling fewer than 4,000,000 megawatt hours of electricity per year. Other defined terms—“bulk-power system,” “cybersecurity threat,” and “defense critical electric infrastructure”—incorporate by reference the definitions in the Federal Power Act (sections 215(a) and 215A(a)) and the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (section 2200).

Subsection (b) directs the Secretary of Energy to maintain the Program, providing technical assistance and awarding funding (grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes) to eligible entities for cybersecurity threat protection, detection, response, and recovery. Subsection (c) states the Program’s objectives: deploying advanced cybersecurity technologies for electric utility systems and increasing eligible-entity participation in cybersecurity threat information-sharing programs.

Subsection (d) prescribes award mechanics. The Secretary shall, subject to the availability of appropriations, provide technical assistance and award funding on a competitive or noncompetitive basis; develop criteria for such assistance and awards; may enter into agreements to further section (c) objectives; and shall establish a process to ensure all eligible entities are informed of Program opportunities. The Secretary must give priority for funding and technical assistance to entities that have limited cybersecurity resources, own assets critical to bulk-power-system reliability, or own or operate defense critical electric infrastructure.

Subsection (e) provides that information shared under the Program with the federal government or state, tribal, or local governments is deemed voluntarily shared and exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552) and all analogous state, tribal, and local open-government, open-records, and sunshine laws.

Subsection (f) authorizes to be appropriated $250,000,000 for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 to carry out the section. No direct appropriation is made, and the bill contains no separate effective date, sunset clause, or additional conditions precedent, taking effect upon enactment.
